newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: FORECAST-Nampak year earnings set to rise.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Nampak year earnings set to rise.

text.p: South Africa's packaging giant Nampak Ltd is set to post a healthy rise in year earnings on Thursday as it battles against rising raw materials prices and tough markets, analysts said on Friday.

Analysts polled by Reuters forecast earnings per share rising to between 103 and 120 cents a share in the year to September 30 from 91 cents in 1995. They expected a dividend of between 37 and 44 cents from 35 cents before.
They said higher raw materials prices and a general economic slowdown in world markets would cap Nampak's profit rise.
"It won't be a really dramatic rise as a lot of their raw materials prices are high and there has been a slow down of demand in their markets," said an analyst who asked not to be identified.

But the firm, the second largest packaging company in the southern hemisphere, has earned market praise for the tight control of its management team and the steps it has taken to boost efficiency, shed staff and cut costs, analysts said.
"The company has really impressed the market," said another analyst.

Despite its tough economic environment the firm has expanded its operations abroad. In June it paid out seven million rand for a controlling stake in Malawi's biggest packaging company Packaging Industries (Malawi) Ltd.

The firm has also this year embarked on a major capital expenditure programme aimed at boosting production. The benefits of this will not show through this year, but will profit the firm in the future, analysts said.

"It is not going to help them now, but it will in the next five years. For an investor Nampak is a great two-year view stock, but it is not a quick upturn stock," said Mark Rule, paper and packaging analyst at Frankel Pollak.
